title: Conversational Marketing Guide: How to Choose the Right Marketing & SEO Platform
description: Practical conversational marketing guidance with workflow design, measurement, data controls, and implementation checks.
author: Emily Nakamura

sections.title: Define the conversation's purpose
sections.body: Identify the customer question or decision the conversation should support: product discovery, lead qualification, support, onboarding, or account assistance. Decide when automation is appropriate and when a human should take over. Write down what a successful interaction looks like and which outcomes the system is allowed to influence. A chatbot should not be introduced merely because competitors have one.

sections.title: Design clear handoff rules
sections.body: Define which intents can be handled automatically, which require a human, and what context transfers with the conversation. Test ambiguous requests, repeated questions, angry customers, requests to delete data, and cases outside business hours. Make escalation visible and ensure the user does not have to repeat information. If the system cannot answer, it should say so and offer a useful next step rather than inventing a response.

sections.title: Connect data and respect preferences
sections.body: Map how conversation records connect to CRM, support, marketing automation, and customer profiles. Decide which fields are collected, why they are needed, and how consent and preferences propagate. Test duplicate contacts, shared devices, existing customers, and deletion requests. Do not collect sensitive data in a chat transcript unless the workflow and controls explicitly support it.

sections.title: Evaluate response quality
sections.body: Test the conversation against real questions, including misspellings, multiple intents, missing information, and unsupported requests. Review whether answers are accurate, clear, and grounded in approved content. For AI-powered replies, test prompt injection, fabricated claims, and escalation behavior. Keep a review process for content updates so the assistant does not continue using outdated product or pricing information.

sections.title: Measure the full experience
sections.body: Track resolution rate, successful handoffs, time to answer, abandoned conversations, repeat contacts, customer satisfaction, and downstream conversion where appropriate. Separate automation completion from actual issue resolution. Compare with a baseline and review a sample of conversations qualitatively. Avoid optimizing only for lead capture if the result is irrelevant leads or a worse customer experience.

sections.title: Check privacy, security, and access
sections.body: Review transcript retention, redaction, permissions, exports, vendor data use, and the handling of personal or payment information. Ensure agents see only the conversations needed for their role. Verify how a customer can request correction or deletion. Consult qualified privacy or legal guidance for applicable consent and notice requirements.

sections.title: Plan operations and cost
sections.body: Include seats, conversation volume, AI usage, messaging channels, integrations, human support coverage, and content maintenance. Verify current plan limits and overage rules. Assign owners for conversation design, escalation, data quality, and incident response. Test what happens when the messaging provider or CRM integration is unavailable.

sections.title: Go-live checklist
sections.body: Pilot one use case with a clear success metric, approved knowledge sources, safe fallback, human handoff, and data controls. Review failures and customer feedback before expanding. Keep a named owner for ongoing tuning and regularly retire flows that no longer match customer needs.

sections.title: Test handoff quality before launch
sections.body: Create test conversations for a straightforward question, an ambiguous request, an out-of-scope question, a complaint, and a request to speak to a person. Verify that the bot does not promise unavailable outcomes, collect unnecessary personal data, or keep a customer trapped in automation. Check whether the human agent receives the conversation history and the reason for escalation. Define who reviews failed conversations and how approved answers are updated when policies or products change.
